greeting.name: Basic Greeting Component
greeting.description: Create a Greeting component that displays a personalized message with an optional name prop.
hints: Accept an optional `name` prop with default "Guest"
Render the full text `Hello, [name]!` inside a single element
Tests use `getByText('Hello, Alice!')` — the exact string must appear in one element

user-card.name: User Card with Multiple Props
user-card.description: Create a UserCard component that displays name, email, and age with typed props.
hints: Render `name`, `email`, and `age` — **each in its own element** (e.g. three separate `<span>`s)
The age must include the prefix `Age: ` — render `Age: {age}`
Tests use `getByText('John Doe')`, which requires the whole element's text to equal `John Doe` (nothing else)

todo-list.name: Todo List (Arrays & Keys)
todo-list.description: Render a list of todos with proper key management and completion status.
hints: Render a `<ul>` — tests use `getByRole('list')` which expects a `<ul>` (or `<ol>`)
Render each todo's `text` inside its own `<li>` with a unique `key` prop
Each todo has a `completed` boolean — React skips booleans when rendering, so map it to a visible value (e.g. `{completed ? '✓' : '⏳'}`)
When `todos` is empty, the `<ul>` must have zero children

counter.name: Counter with State
counter.description: Create a counter with increment and decrement buttons using the useState hook.
hints: Use `useState<number>(0)` for the count
Display the count as `Count: {n}` — the `Count: ` prefix is required
Two `<button>` elements whose **text** contains `increment` and `decrement` (case-insensitive)

status-message.name: Conditional Rendering
status-message.description: Implement conditional rendering for loading, error, and data states.
hints: Priority: `isLoading` > `error` > `data`. Return `null` if none are set
Loading state: render any element whose text contains `loading` (e.g. `Loading...`)

Error & data states: render the prop's string value **with no extra text around it**. The tests do exact matches like `getByText('Something went wrong')` — `
Error: {error}
` would fail because the element's text becomes 'Error: Something went wrong'

action-button.name: Event Handler Button
action-button.description: Create a button that handles click events via a callback prop.
hints: Render a real `<button>` element (tests use `getByRole('button')`)
The button's text must be exactly the `text` prop value
Wire `onClick={onClick}` directly on the `<button>` — don't wrap it

contact-form.name: Controlled Input Form
contact-form.description: Create a form with controlled inputs for name and email, handling submission.
hints: Use `<label htmlFor="x">` paired with `<input id="x" />` so `getByLabelText` finds each input by name/email
Add `role="form"` to your `<form>` element — `getByRole('form')` needs it
Submit button must have text containing `submit` (e.g. `<button type="submit">Submit</button>`)
On submit: call `e.preventDefault()`, then `onSubmit({ name, email })`

filtered-list.name: Filtered List with State
filtered-list.description: Create a searchable list that filters items based on a search term.
hints: Search input must have a `placeholder` containing `search` (e.g. `placeholder="Search"`)
Render each filtered item's `name` in its own element so `getByText('Apple')` can find it
Filter: keep items whose `name.toLowerCase()` includes `searchTerm.toLowerCase()`

counter-functional.name: useState with Functional Updates
counter-functional.description: Create a counter using functional updates to prevent stale state.
hints: Use `useState<number>(0)` for the count
Display the count as `Count: {n}` — the `Count: ` prefix is required
Two `<button>` elements whose **text** contains `increment` and `decrement` (case-insensitive)
Use **functional updates** so rapid clicks all apply: `setCount(c => c + 1)`

data-fetching.name: useEffect Data Fetching
data-fetching.description: Fetch data on mount with loading, error, and success states.
hints: Three states: `loading`, `data`, `error` — track with `useState`. Render-time priority: loading → error → data
Loading: render any element whose text contains `loading` (e.g. `Loading...`)
Success: render the fetched user's `name` and `email` — each in its own element so `getByText` finds them exactly
Error: render any element whose text contains `error`
Cleanup: in `useEffect` return, set a `cancelled = true` flag so you don't `setState` after unmount

theme-context.name: useContext Theme Provider
theme-context.description: Create a theme context with provider, consumer hook, and toggle component.
hints: ThemeProvider: `useState<'light' | 'dark'>('light')`, expose `{ theme, toggleTheme }` via the `ThemeContext.Provider`
useTheme: read the context with `useContext(ThemeContext)`. If it's `undefined`, `throw new Error(...)` so misuse outside the provider crashes loudly
ThemeToggle: render the current theme text (containing `light` or `dark`) and a button whose text contains `toggle`

focus-input.name: useRef Focus Management
focus-input.description: Use useRef to create an input reference and a button that focuses it.
hints: Use `useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)` and attach it: `<input ref={inputRef} />`
Render a button whose text contains `focus` (e.g. `Focus the input`) that calls `inputRef.current?.focus()`
Tests use `getByRole('textbox')` for the input and `getByText(/focus/i)` for the button

filtered-list-memo.name: useMemo Derived Data
filtered-list-memo.description: Use useMemo to optimize filtering and sorting of a list.
hints: Accept three props: `items: Item[]`, `filter: string`, `sortBy: 'name' | 'value'`
Filter: keep items where `item.category === filter`
Sort: by `name` use `a.name.localeCompare(b.name)`; by `value` use `a.value - b.value`
Wrap the filter+sort in `useMemo(() => …, [items, filter, sortBy])` and render each result as `<li>` inside a `<ul>`

callback-parent.name: useCallback Stable References
callback-parent.description: Use useCallback to prevent unnecessary re-renders of memoized children.
hints: MemoizedChild: `React.memo` around a component that renders `<button onClick={onClick}>{label}</button>`
ParentWithCallback: two `useState` slices (e.g. `count` and `otherState`). Two buttons that toggle each
Wrap the handler in `useCallback(() => {…}, [])` so its reference stays stable across renders, and pass it to `MemoizedChild` as `onClick`

todo-reducer.name: useReducer Todo Management
todo-reducer.description: Implement a full todo app with useReducer for complex state management.
hints: Reducer: handle four action types — `ADD_TODO`, `TOGGLE_TODO`, `DELETE_TODO`, `CLEAR_COMPLETED`. Always return a new state object
ADD_TODO: append `{ id: state.nextId, text: action.payload, completed: false }` and increment `nextId`
TOGGLE_TODO: flip `completed` on the todo whose id matches `action.payload`. DELETE_TODO: filter that id out. CLEAR_COMPLETED: keep only `!completed`
TodoApp: input must have a `placeholder` containing `add todo` (e.g. `placeholder="Add todo"`). Don't dispatch ADD_TODO if the input is empty/whitespace
Each todo row needs a `<input type="checkbox">` (for `getByRole('checkbox')`) and a button whose text contains `delete`. Plus one button whose text contains `clear completed`
